newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK HALTS SECONDARY ZUNK BOND AUCTIONS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK HALTS SECONDARY ZUNK BOND AUCTIONS.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) will not hold an auction of bad loan or ZUNK bonds auction next week mainly due to the lack of interest from the seller side, a central bank official said on Wednesday.

"We will not hold new secondary ZUNK auctions for a time being after no deals were struck at the two auctions this week and the last," Nikolina Micheva, head of Fiscal Services department at the central bank told Reuters.
There were no deals at the second ZUNK bond secondary auction of issues 98/93 and 97/94 held by the BNB on Tuesday because of broadly divergent buy and sell prices, the BNB said in a statement.
At the first secondary auction of those issues held by the BNB on July 15 there were no deals either.
Bids amounted to 8.205 billion levs for issue 98/93 of lev-denominated ZUNK bonds but there were no offers. The minimum bid price was 63 percent of par and the maximum 70 percent, the BNB said.

Bids for $19.7 million and offers of $2.0 million worth of the dollar-denominated ZUNK bonds issue 97/94 were placed but there were no trades becuase the highest bid was 70 percent of par while the lowest offer was 70.75 percent.

But interbank secondary trade in ZUNKs was going on unaffected. Dollar-denominated ZUNKs with a total par of $622,300 traded at 68.75 and 69.50 percent of par on Tuesday and 22.359 million levs of lev-denominated ZUNKs changed hands at 715.57 percent of par.
Dealers said the auctions would continue to attract little interest unless trading rules were made more flexible.
"The auctions parallel the interbank secondary market but fail to offer more attractive trading options for banks," said a dealer.

"If primary dealers were allowed to place more orders on their behalf and on behalf of their clients, trade will get livelier because there will be a wider price margin," a large state-owned commercial bank dealer said.

Only financial institutions that are primary dealers in government securities were allowed to take part at the auctions so far, placing only one order on their behalf and one order on behalf of each of their clients.
Other companies, individuals and financial institutions could participate at the auctions through orders placed with the primary dealers.
The lack of direct contact between buyers and sellers in setting prices also prevented them from arriving at an equilibrium price at the auctions, traders said.
Participants at the auctions were required to set a maximum buy price or a minimum sell price.
ZUNK bonds with a par value of 13.482 billion levs and $892 million were in circulation at end-June.

The bonds were issued three years ago to cover unperforming loans extended to state enterprises before 1991. They are accepted as means of payment in local sell-offs at par value. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
